scope.summary: This standard covers the manufacturing process, chemical, and physical requirements for microfine ordinary Portland cement (OPC) as well as microfine sulphate resisting Portland cement. It applies to cement used in specialized applications such as rock grouting, soil stabilization, and underground construction for water leak prevention.

certification_and_marking.disclaimer: No mandatory BIS product certification (such as the ISI Mark) is strictly required within the code of practice text itself for purchasing or using the cement. However, to guarantee quality and safe usage, the standard establishes the voluntary BIS Standard Mark scheme alongside critical material testing, storage, and manufacturer certification requirements:

requirements.provision: The microfine cement product may be marked with the Standard Mark under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016.
The manufacturer must ensure conformance and, if requested, provide a certified test certificate to the purchaser within 10 days of testing (28-day compressive results are delivered upon completion).
The manufacturer must provide a certified test report specifying the alkali content of the cement if requested by the purchaser.

Each bag, advice note, or drum must be clearly marked with key details, notably highlighting the requirement for testing microfine cement that is more than 3 months old to check conformance before its use.

Cement stored in bulk at the mill for more than 6 months, or stored in bags locally by a vendor for more than 3 months, must be retested and may be rejected if it fails any physical/chemical parameter.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 16993:2018 is the national standard specification in India for microfine ordinary Portland cement and microfine sulphate resisting Portland cement, developed for high-performance rock grouting, concrete repair, soil stabilization, and underground leak prevention. Unlike standard OPC, this cement requires extremely high particle fineness—requiring a minimum specific surface area of 2000 m²/kg (via Nitrogen adsorption BET method) and tight particle size limits of D50 ≤ 10 µm and D95 ≤ 20 µm (via laser diffraction analyzer). Physical compliance is tested under high water-cement conditions (1:1 ratio for setting time and bleed limits, and 1:3 mortar with optional superplasticizer for compressive strength). Engineers must ensure that any cement stored in bulk for over 6 months or in bags for over 3 months is retested and confirmed compliant prior to site application.
